text: The 2022 Rugby Europe Championship was the sixth edition of the annual rugby union competition for the top European national teams outside the Six Nations Championship and the 52nd overall iteration of the tournament, encompassing all its previous names such as the FIRA Tournament, Rugby Union European Cup, FIRA Nations Cup, FIRA Trophy, and European Nations Cup. The tournament featured Georgia, The Netherlands, Portugal, Romania, Russia, and Spain. Georgia entered as defending champions, having won all their matches in the 2021 tournament to claim their 13th title and 10th Grand Slam. Russia were disqualified after Week 3 due to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine. This year's championship also served as the second year of the 2023 Rugby World Cup qualifiers for Europe, with the winner and runner-up earning automatic qualification as Europe 1 and Europe 2, respectively, and the third-place team advancing to the final qualification tournament as Europe 3. The touch judges and television match officials included: George Selwood and Mike Woods (England), Rowan Kitt (England); Manuel Bottino and Leonardo Masini (Italy), Emanuele Tomo (Italy); Ludovic Cayre and Stéphane Boyer (France), Denis Grenouillet (France); Federico Vedovelli and Filippo Bertelli (Italy), Stefano Roscini (Italy); Cédric Marchat and Stéphane Crapoix (France), Patrick Pechambert (France); Oisin Quinn and Nigel Correll (Ireland), Leo Colgan (Ireland); Riccardo Angelucci and Simone Boaretto (Italy), Alan Falzone (Italy); Graeme Ormiston and Jonny Perriam (Scotland), Neil Paterson (Scotland); Gareth Newman and Mark Butcher (Wales), Elgan Williams (Wales); David Beun and Christophe Bultet (France), Eric Briquet-Campin (France); Ru Campbell and Bob Nevins (Scotland), Andrew Mac Menemy (Scotland); Ben Breakspear and Ian Davies (Wales), Jon Mason (Wales).
